title: Structural Trustworthiness Ontology

dispositions.target_leakage: The nominated target is a member of the relation's support; the posed task is answerable by arithmetic over shipped columns.
dispositions.structural_constraint: The relation lives entirely among non-target columns (for example physics or accounting); charged to feature redundancy, not to leakage.
dispositions.redundancy: A duplicate or near-copy among non-target columns.
dispositions.not_applicable: No nominated target (target-free audit), or the class is target-independent.

roles.input: A stochastic feature with no detected artifact role.
roles.derived_deterministic: A column that is an exact function of other columns.
roles.near_deterministic: A column predictable out-of-sample beyond the near threshold, not captured by an exact relation.
roles.label_component: A column that participates in the target's generating relation.
roles.leaky_feature: A feature (near-)computed from the target (post-outcome) or single-feature dominant.
roles.duplicate: A duplicate or near-copy of another column.
roles.constant: A column with a single non-missing value.
roles.identifier: A near-key column carrying no learnable signal.
roles.no_signal: A column with no usable predictive signal.

reserved_output_symbols.STO-X00: Unclassified suspected structure (open world); scored as an abstention, never as a false positive.
reserved_output_symbols.ABSTAIN: An explicit abstention on a column set.

compatibility: Class identifiers are permanent and are never redefined incompatibly. Adding a class is a MINOR ontology change; removing or redefining a class is MAJOR. Deprecated classes are retained with a replacement pointer and the version of deprecation.
extension_policy: New classes are proposed through the governance change process, must specify every register field and a gold type, and must not overlap an existing class without an explicit relationship note.

classes.name: Linear identity
classes.definition: A column is an exact affine function of one or more other columns: a linear combination of the support columns equals a constant on every non-missing row.
classes.inclusion_criteria: The affine relation holds on all non-missing rows to within the exactness tolerance.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Relations holding only on a subsample; relations explained by a single duplicated column (use STO-A08); homogeneous sign-only balances (use STO-A02).
classes.example: cost = power * tariff with a constant tariff.
classes.counterexample: A noisy regression with residual variance above tolerance.
relationships: specializes to STO-A08 when the support has size two with unit coefficient

classes.name: Conservation or balance constraint
classes.definition: A homogeneous linear identity whose coefficients are all in {+1, -1}: a signed sum of columns equal to a constant, typically zero.
classes.inclusion_criteria: STO-A01 holds and the coefficients are unit-signed.

classes.name: Multiplicative (power-law) identity
classes.definition: A column is an exact product of powers of strictly-positive columns: an affine identity holds in the logarithm of the support.
classes.inclusion_criteria: The log-space affine relation holds on all non-missing rows to the exactness tolerance.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Relations requiring non-positive values; additive relations (use STO-A01).

classes.name: Regime-affine identity
classes.definition: A column equals an affine function of numeric columns plus an additive offset that depends on the level of a categorical column.
classes.scope: A numeric target column and a low-cardinality categorical regime column.
classes.inclusion_criteria: After removing per-level means an affine identity holds to the near tolerance and the per-level offsets are non-degenerate.
classes.exclusion_criteria: A plain STO-A01 that already explains the column without regime offsets.
classes.counterexample: An affine relation with no categorical dependence.

classes.name: Functional dependency
classes.definition: The value of a discrete column is determined by the value of a determinant column (or minimal set), up to a small violation rate.
classes.inclusion_criteria: The g3 violation rate is at most the FD tolerance, the dependent is non-degenerate (modal frequency below the modal cap), and the determinant is not a near-key.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Dependencies onto near-constant columns (they restate imbalance); key-like determinants.
classes.counterexample: CODE -> STATUS where STATUS is 99.9 percent one value.
relationships: discrete analog of a deterministic relation

classes.name: Rule-derived discrete label
classes.definition: A discrete column is, to high fidelity, a deterministic rule (a shallow decision function of thresholds and categories) over other columns.
classes.scope: Discrete columns with between two and a small number of levels.
classes.inclusion_criteria: A rule of bounded depth reproduces the column at fidelity at least the rule threshold, removes at least half of the majority-class error, and for near-constant columns only a perfect rule qualifies.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Fidelity attributable only to class imbalance; exact univariate thresholds (use STO-A07).
classes.example: Machine failure = rules(TWF, HDF, PWF, OSF).
classes.counterexample: A label with genuine irreducible noise.
relationships: adjudicated because the qualifying rule depends on a learned function class

classes.name: Threshold or sign label
classes.definition: A binary column equals the indicator of a numeric column crossing a fixed threshold (a perfect univariate separation).
classes.scope: A binary column and a numeric feature.
classes.inclusion_criteria: The two classes occupy disjoint ranges of the numeric column (a separating threshold exists), each class having at least the minimum count.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Separations on ultra-rare classes; approximate separations.
classes.counterexample: A binary label whose class ranges overlap.
relationships: special case of STO-A06 with an exact single-feature threshold

classes.name: Duplicate or near-copy column
classes.definition: Two columns are equal up to sign and negligible jitter (correlation magnitude at or above the duplicate threshold), or two non-numeric columns are identical as strings.
classes.inclusion_criteria: Correlation magnitude at least the duplicate threshold, or exact string equality.
classes.counterexample: Two correlated but distinct sensors at r = 0.95.

classes.name: Duplicate rows
classes.definition: Exact repeated records in the table.
classes.scope: Whole row; support is the reserved <ROWS> token.
classes.inclusion_criteria: The duplicate-row fraction exceeds the duplicate-row threshold.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Near-duplicates below the exactness rule (report as STO-X00 if desired).
classes.counterexample: A table with no exact repeats.

classes.name: Constant column
classes.definition: A column takes a single non-missing value, or is entirely missing.
classes.inclusion_criteria: Cardinality at most one over non-missing values.
classes.counterexample: A column with two rare distinct values.

classes.name: Lattice or quantization marginal
classes.definition: The distinct values of a numeric column lie on an arithmetic lattice (integer multiples of a common step), with the distinct-value count well below the row count.
classes.inclusion_criteria: Sorted successive differences are integer multiples of the minimum positive step to within the lattice tolerance, and the distinct-value count is below half the row count.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Naturally discrete counts that are semantically integer; continuous columns.
classes.counterexample: A floating measurement with dense unique values.

classes.name: Uniform-sampled marginal
classes.definition: A numeric column's empirical distribution over its observed range is indistinguishable from uniform (a design-of-experiments input signature).
classes.inclusion_criteria: The Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic against the uniform on the observed range is below the uniform tolerance.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Columns with too few non-missing values.
classes.example: An input swept uniformly across a range.

classes.name: Schedule or row-order leakage
classes.definition: The target (or a key column) exhibits strong serial structure in file order, indicating blocked or scheduled rows that are not exchangeable.
classes.scope: The target column in file order; support is the reserved <ROWS> token with the target named in evidence.
classes.inclusion_criteria: The lag-1 autocorrelation magnitude of the encoded target exceeds the autocorrelation threshold.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Independent and identically distributed targets; tables whose row order is explicitly randomized and documented.
classes.example: BATADAL attack windows in contiguous blocks.

classes.name: Cross-split contamination
classes.definition: Records appear in more than one released split of the same dataset.
classes.scope: The pair of released tables; support is the reserved <ROWS> token.
classes.inclusion_criteria: At least one record of the companion split is present in the primary table under exact match on shared columns, rounded to a stated precision.
classes.example: 610 NSL-KDD test rows present verbatim in the training file.

classes.name: Single-feature dominance
classes.definition: A single feature alone achieves near-perfect predictive performance on the target, over the majority baseline, indicating a shortcut or leak.
classes.inclusion_criteria: A baseline-relative single-feature score at or above the single-feature threshold.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Dominance attributable to degenerate slices or class imbalance (scores must be baseline-relative and computed on non-degenerate slices).
classes.example: A feature that is a noisy copy of the target.
classes.counterexample: A feature with moderate univariate signal.
relationships: often co-occurs with STO-A01 or STO-A08 when the feature is a target descendant

classes.name: Residual near-determinism
classes.definition: A column is predictable out-of-sample from the others beyond a high threshold by a general (possibly nonlinear) learner, and is not already explained by an A-class relation.
classes.inclusion_criteria: An out-of-sample skill (baseline-relative for classification, coefficient of determination for regression) at or above the determinism threshold, with the column not covered by STO-A01 through STO-A08.
classes.exclusion_criteria: Columns fully explained by an A-class identity (report the A-class instead).
classes.example: A nonlinear derived column outside the algebraic classes.
relationships: complements the A-classes for out-of-class deterministic structure
